subject.title: fix: 429 errors without rate-limit wording skip the same-model retry

question: Should leading HTTP 429 provider errors that are not long-window, quota, billing, or usage-limit shaped use the existing same-model rate-limit retry ladder before auth-profile rotation or model fallback?
rationale: The patch is narrow and proven, but it changes fallback timing for an error class that can come from multiple providers and overlaps with adjacent retry-classifier work.

options.title: Accept bounded leading-429 retry
options.body: Treat eligible leading 429s as short-window throttles and merge once exact-head checks and maintainer review are complete.

options.title: Sequence after retry cleanup
options.body: Land the session retry-classifier refactor first, then rebase this PR so both helper changes coexist cleanly.

options.title: Hold for narrower policy
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want provider-specific classification before changing generic leading-429 retry timing.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded leading-429 retry
recommendation.body: Treat eligible leading 429s as short-window throttles and merge once exact-head checks and maintainer review are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent same-model retry and shared helper history and are the best available owner for this compatibility-sensitive retry-policy choice.
